description.value: Greater Vancouver regional transit. Bikes accepted on all modes: buses (exterior front rack, 2-bike max), SeaBus (up to 6 bikes at peak), SkyTrain Canada Line (1 bike/car, all times), Expo and Millennium lines (2 bikes/car), and West Coast Express (2 bikes/car). No bike fee on any mode. On the Expo and Millennium lines, bikes aren't allowed on westbound trains 7-9 am or eastbound trains 4-6 pm on weekdays; Canada Line has no time restrictions. E-bikes ride on the bus rack with the lithium battery removed and carried on board, bike under 25 kg (55 lb); scooter and moped-style e-bikes aren't allowed. In summer (mid-June to early September), the seasonal 900 Bike Bus runs Fridays, weekends, and holidays between Bridgeport Station and the Tsawwassen ferry terminal with room for 10 bikes, hourly and timed to ferry sailings, a bike-friendly way through the Massey Tunnel, which you can't cycle. New to putting your bike on transit? It is easier than it looks, and it opens up a lot of BC. TransLink's Bikes on Transit page walks you through it: short videos on loading the front rack, etiquette tips, and guidance for every kind of bike. Worth a look before your first trip.

Accommodates bicycles.detail: Bikes free on bus (2-bike front racks), SkyTrain, SeaBus, West Coast Express; peak-direction limits on Expo/Millennium

E-bikes OK.detail: battery removed and carried on board, bike under 25 kg; no scooter/moped-style
